title: SQS Queue Depth and Age of Oldest Message

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudwatch` events with `namespace="AWS/SQS" (metric_name="ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible" OR metric_name="ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage")` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.24 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudwatch` traffic without `namespace="AWS/SQS" (metric_name="ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible" OR metric_name="ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage")`. Confirm UC-4.1.24 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/SQS" (metric_name="ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible" OR metric_name="ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage")

| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.24_sqs_queue_depth_and_age_24"

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `metric_name` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Collect SQS metrics. Alert when queue depth exceeds threshold (e.g. 1000) or age of oldest message > 5 minutes. Monitor dead-letter queue (ApproximateNumberOfMessagesDelayed) separately.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/SQS" (metric_name="ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible" OR metric_name="ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage")
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.24_sqs_queue_depth_and_age_24"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch` in `index=aws` to detect sqs queue depth and age of oldest message. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon CloudWatch console Metrics for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `metric_name` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_24_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (depth, age by queue), Single value (oldest message age), Table (queue, depth)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of sqs queue depth and age of oldest message so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
